input: Rotate and balance the tires before the road trip

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The road trip departure date sets a hard deadline that determines how urgently the appointment must be booked and how much lead time is available.
Knowing whether the user plans to go to a shop or do it themselves completely changes the steps involved — scheduling vs. gathering tools and equipment.
If the user already has a preferred mechanic or shop, the plan focuses on booking; if not, it needs to include finding and vetting a service provider.
The user may want only rotation and balance, or may also need an inspection of tread depth, tire pressure, and overall tire condition — which affects time and cost.
Transportation while the car is being serviced (e.g., waiting at the shop, needing a ride, or a loaner vehicle) is a practical step that must be planned.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like — e.g., a shop receipt, specific vibration eliminated, or tires confirmed road-trip-ready — shapes what the user considers 'done.'
Budget sensitivity matters: the user may want the cheapest option, a trusted brand-name shop, or a dealership, which affects where and how to book the service.

gold.taskTitle: Rotate and balance tires before road trip
gold.taskDescription: Get the vehicle's tires rotated and balanced in preparation for an upcoming road trip.

questions.title: When exactly does your road trip depart?
questions.description: Identify the departure date to set the deadline for completing the tire service and determine how urgently the appointment needs to be scheduled.

questions.title: Will you use a shop or do it yourself?
questions.description: Determine whether the plan should focus on booking a professional service appointment or on gathering the tools and steps for a DIY rotation and balance.

questions.title: Do you have a go-to mechanic or shop already?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a preferred service provider so the plan either skips or includes a step for researching and choosing a shop.

questions.title: Should any other tire checks be included too?
questions.description: Clarify whether the scope covers only rotation and balance, or also includes tread depth inspection, tire pressure check, or overall tire condition assessment.

questions.title: How will you get around while the car is serviced?
questions.description: Address the logistics of transportation during the service appointment — whether the user will wait at the shop, need a ride, or require a loaner vehicle.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Understand what 'done well' means — for example, no vibration while driving, a written service record, tires confirmed safe for highway miles, or a specific mileage target met.

questions.title: Do you have a budget in mind for this service?
questions.description: Gauge price sensitivity to tailor recommendations toward the most affordable option, a trusted national chain, or a dealership service center.
